gaps.title: Complete closure requires every named issuer authority class
gaps.close_criteria: A complete bundle may contain multiple submissions for one gap and is eligible only when every authority class listed by the canonical contract is represented by a cryptographically valid submission. Within one gap, authority seats use distinct trust-registry key IDs and distinct identity/organization pairs; one omnipotent key or identity cannot fill multiple seats. Partial bundles report missing classes and never produce all_authority_owned_gaps_closed=true.

gaps.title: Final signed review roster and acceptance context are removal-resistant
gaps.close_criteria: Every accepted bundle requires every final signed review artifact to carry the same schema-v1 G10 closure manifest. The manifest binds the explicit policy ID/revision, ordered final reviewer roster, acceptance state, reviewed_at, decision_reference and limitations. Because each review artifact digest is in the reviewer Ed25519 statement, removing, adding, replacing or reordering a final reviewer, changing final acceptance context, or substituting another policy revision fails validation. External governance still determines whether every accountable review was admitted to the final roster.

gaps.title: Complete-closure semantics are versioned and issuer claims are authority-scoped
gaps.close_criteria: The canonical external-evidence contract revision is 2026-09-02-g10-quorum-1 and explicitly identifies its G9 predecessor, all-class quorum mode, exact class-scoped claim mode, distinct authority seats and review-manifest profile. Required claims are a validated disjoint partition across the named authority classes for each gap. Each issuer may sign exactly its assigned claims; missing or cross-scope claims fail before acceptance. Contract revision is inside issuer and reviewer signature preimages, and policy ID/revision are inside review-set and acceptance-context digests, so a G10 package cannot be accepted by the older G9 semantic revision. The policy module itself, the acceptance-module alias, the CLI and the package-level validator all resolve to the same immutable, aggregate-bounded validation-snapshot entrypoint; explicitly importing complete_closure cannot bypass filesystem custody.

gaps.title: Repository CI discovers every committed accepted immutable successor
gaps.close_criteria: Repository qualification recursively inspects bounded regular files under evidence/external by canonical envelope content rather than only matching a top-level bundle.json filename. Candidate discovery uses O_NOFOLLOW and one stable descriptor whose lexical, opened and post-read device/inode/mode/size/mtime/ctime identities agree; symbolic links, ordinary replacement between lstat and open, special objects, oversized files, unsupported no-follow APIs and unstable reads are never promoted. Every discovered envelope whose contract_id is canonical and acceptance.state is accepted is mapped to its enclosing custody root and revalidated as complete and accepted under a protected out-of-band trust-registry pin. Filename, extension, nesting, successor placement, or a discovery-time replacement cannot hide or inject an accepted package.

gaps.title: Authority-bearing validation cannot inherit caller clock or executable authority
gaps.close_criteria: The package API, direct complete_closure module and executable CLI use the trusted current system clock and the canonical OpenSSL command. They reject a caller-supplied validation time and any custom OpenSSL executable before reading evidence. The CLI exposes no cryptographic-binary override. A private deterministic clock hook is absent from __all__, used only by the historical qualification fixture, and still rejects custom OpenSSL selection. Expired, revoked or future-dated evidence cannot be made current by public argument injection, and an attacker-selected executable cannot manufacture cryptographic success through an authority-bearing entrypoint.

gaps.title: Issuer and reviewer signatures bind canonical contract semantics
gaps.close_criteria: Every issuer and reviewer canonical Ed25519 preimage contains a contract-binding statement with contract ID, declared revision and the canonical SHA-256 of the complete current contract object. The evidence-set digest carries the same binding. A contract whose revision string is unchanged but whose authority classes, claim partition, review rules, closure rule or any other canonical field changes produces different submission, evidence-set and review digests and invalidates existing signatures. A caller-supplied revision that differs from the current contract bytes fails before signing or verification.
